summary: Sustained 429 spikes after credit reconciliation during simultaneous bulk backfill and low-latency webhooks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ScribeAI reports sustained 429 responses across a subset of API keys immediately following a tenant credit reconciliation event (automatic refill) that occurred 2026-03-10 00:05 UTC. The tenant was simultaneously running a long-running bulk embedding backfill and high-frequency webhook-driven chat inference for low-latency UI actions.

Impact:
- Customer sees 20-40% of requests returning 429 for ~3 hours after refill window.
- Real-time chat flows experienced user-visible failures; bulk backfill jobs retried and slowed throughput.
- Appears to affect only requests routed via the dedicated pool in us-east.

Requested outcome:
- Root cause analysis and mitigation to avoid recurrence during future credit refills and autosyncs.
- Guidance / recommended config to isolate bulk backfills from low-latency routes (rate classes, burst pools, or route separation).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant with scheduled midnight credit refill, kick off a large parallel bulk embedding job (1000 concurrent workers) against the embeddings endpoint.
2) At the same time, run simulated user traffic: 200 RPS of short chat requests (streaming) using multiple short-lived API keys and websocket sessions.
3) Observe behavior immediately after automatic credit refill / tenant reconciliation (00:00-00:10 UTC window).
4) Check responses for 429 and compare rate-limit headers and refill timestamps in origin vs edge proxies.
logs_snippets: 2026-03-10T00:05:14Z edge-proxy: incoming_request key=ak_live_*** route=chat-low-latency status=429 X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 X-RateLimit-Reset=300
investigation_notes: Initial triage: pattern correlates timing of 'tenant credit reconciliation' event with onset of 429s across both chat and embeddings routes.
Hypothesis A: Refill applied at origin but edge token buckets did not align immediately, producing a transient double-counting or negative refill delta at edge proxies.
Hypothesis B: Bulk ingest workers held long-lived HTTP/2 connections encouraging token-window exhaustion at connection-level accounting despite tenant-level refill.

Observed: Rate-limit headers reported X-RateLimit-Reset values varying between edge and origin by up to 270s during spike window; origin showed positive refill but per-connection counters at edges were zeroed or stale.
Related signals: dedicated-pool autoscaler showed no GPU shortage; CPU and networking within pool were nominal. No 5xx spike, only 429s and retry waves.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:15 — Support (Ava Chen): Received initial report from customer and asked for request_id samples and approximate timestamps. Customer provided sample ids and traces.

2026-03-10 03:04 — SRE (Diego Martin): Correlated provided request_ids to edge logs. Found that edge token windows were not refreshed for the connection pool that handled the bulk-worker fans after refill. Suspect refill race with health-check probes.

2026-03-10 05:22 — Support (Ava Chen): Sent mitigation steps to customer to stagger bulk ingest start times away from refill window; asked if they can pin bulk to 'bulk-ingest' route with lower priority.

2026-03-11 09:00 — Customer (ScribeAI - Priya Rao): Implemented staggered start and saw reduction of 429s to <2% during next refill. Customer requests formal config recommendations and whether platform can avoid future edge-origin window drift.

2026-03-12 11:40 — SRE (Diego Martin): Proposed short-term workaround: configure separate route id and priority class for bulk backfills, enable route isolation via Console (create dedicated low-priority route with its own burst pool). Long term: engineering to investigate edge refill sync logic for dedicated pools.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer staggered bulk job starts away from refill window and pinned bulk traffic to a separate low-priority route. This reduced 429 rates significantly on the next refill.

Next steps: Engineering to open a follow-up (INT) to evaluate edge-origin refill synchronization for dedicated pools and consider adding a configurable cooldown window after tenant refill to avoid immediate heavy fanout. Support will close this ticket after code-level follow-up is created and customer confirms stable behavior in two refill cycles.
